text:
alex: ACME just escalated: they want tenant routing + enterprise SSO moved into the v1 commitment. They said it's a commercial blocker for renewal.
maya: Clarify: enterprise SSO = OIDC + SCIM + audit streaming?
alex: Yep, their note lists OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and streaming audit logs to their SIEM. They asked for mid-June delivery.
simon: Our public v1 is July. Mid-June GA is optimistic.
emily: If we promise mid-June, we need to cut scope elsewhere. What can we reasonably deprioritize?
alfred: From ACME: analytics retention and promo dashboard are negotiable. They need login/provisioning first.
maya: Quick eng estimate: SCIM + edge cases 5w, OIDC + auth plumbing 2w, infra (VPC/KMS + exports) 2w, QA/compliance 2w. ~11w serial, maybe 7	6w parallel.
sam: Also legal SLA negotiation often adds 1w. Could be parallel but sometimes blocks sign-off.
nora: Suggest middle ground: offer an OIDC-first canary (feature-flag) by Jun 15 with audit exports, then full SCIM GA in v1 (Jul 15).
simon: SCIM is the big integration/test burden. Removing it from the canary buys time.
emily: Audit export is light: S3/Kinesis sink + small adapter for SIEM. Easier to validate.
alex: I pitched an OIDC-first path to ACME; they said they'd consider as long as we commit to SCIM GA and provide audit streaming.
maya: Draft scope for canary: OIDC auth flows for 3 pilot tenants; audit export validated; feature-flag gating; clear rollback. Acceptance criteria: successful login + provisioning via account team, <1% auth errors, logs exported and ingested by their SIEM.
simon: Infra plan: run canary in eu-west to limit blast radius, short-lived route, dedicated small instance pool, route traffic only for pilot orgs. Autoscale target minimal.
emily: I'll write the runbook: deploy steps, feature flag toggle, smoke tests, rollback markers, and dashboard metrics: auth success rate, latencies, export backlog.
maya: Proposed dev assignment: two engineers to SSO canary (OIDC + exports), one engineer slows analytics work. That moves promo dashboard to v1.1.
sam: Legal will need SLA language; I'll loop in counsel and try to get draft within 5 business days.
alfred: ACME wants weekly checkpoints; I'll set those up. They also want a firm GA date for SCIM.
nora: Formal decision (capture here): Deliver OIDC-canary Jun 15 (feature-flagged, 3 pilots), SCIM GA by Jul 15 in v1. Cuts: promo dashboard and extended analytics retention -> v1.1. Risks: SLA negotiation, SCIM test coverage, and on-call load during canary.
alex: Action list: maya -> PRD for canary by EOD; simon -> infra plan + canary routing by Friday; emily -> runbook + metrics by Friday; sam -> legal SLA kickoff; alfred -> schedule ACME weekly checkpoints. I'll confirm canary acceptance criteria with customer today.
maya: ack :thumbsup:
emily: ack
simon: ack
jira-bot: Created SSO-4512 "tenant-sso-canary" and linked dependencies — https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/SSO-4512
alex: We'll update product roadmap doc and communicate changes to stakeholders after PRD review. Closing here once ACME confirms canary OK.
